verses.greek: Ἦν δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων, Νικόδημος ὄνομα αὐτῷ, ἄρχων τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
verses.dgt: Now there was a man from the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
verses.literal: There was now a man of the Pharisees, Nicodemus name to him, a ruler of the Jews.

verses.greek: οὗτος ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐλήλυθας διδάσκαλος· οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται ταῦτα τὰ σημεῖα ποιεῖν ἃ σὺ ποιεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.dgt: He came to him at night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.”
verses.literal: He came to Him by night and said to Him; Rabbi, we know that from God You have come a teacher; no one for is able these the signs to do that You yourself do, only unless shall be the God with him.

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν, οὐ δύναται ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.dgt: Jesus answered and said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless someone is born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
verses.literal: Answered Jesus and said to him; Amen Amen I say to you; only unless someone shall be born from above, not he is able to see the kingdom the of God.
notes: ἄνωθεν can mean “from above” and can also carry the sense “again”; Nicodemus’s reply in the next verse plays on that ambiguity.

verses.greek: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Νικόδημος· Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος γεννηθῆναι γέρων ὤν; μὴ δύναται εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ δεύτερον εἰσελθεῖν καὶ γεννηθῆναι;
verses.dgt: Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time and be born?”
verses.literal: Says to Him the Nicodemus; How is able a man to be born old being? Not is he able into the womb of the mother of him a second time to enter and to be born?

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.dgt: Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.”
verses.literal: Answered Jesus; Amen Amen I say to you, only unless someone shall be born of water and of the Spirit, not he is able to enter into the kingdom the of God.
notes: “Born of water and Spirit” translates ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος directly; the phrase’s theological interpretation is not expanded in the translation itself.

verses.greek: τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς σάρξ ἐστιν, καὶ τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος πνεῦμά ἐστιν.
verses.dgt: What has been born of the flesh is flesh, and what has been born of the Spirit is spirit.
verses.literal: That born of the flesh flesh is, and that born of the Spirit spirit is.

verses.greek: μὴ θαυμάσῃς ὅτι εἶπόν σοι Δεῖ ὑμᾶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν.
verses.dgt: Do not be amazed that I said to you, ‘You all must be born from above.’
verses.literal: Not may do wonder that I said to you; It is necessary for you all to be born from above.

verses.greek: τὸ πνεῦμα ὅπου θέλει πνεῖ, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἀκούεις, ἀλλʼ οὐκ οἶδας πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει· οὕτως ἐστὶν πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος.
verses.dgt: The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit.
verses.literal: The wind where it wishes blows, and the sound of it You hear but not you know from where it comes and where it goes; thus is everyone who born of the Spirit.
notes: πνεῦμα can mean “wind” or “spirit.” The verse deliberately moves from the wind image to being born of the Spirit.

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Νικόδημος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πῶς δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι;
verses.dgt: Nicodemus answered and said to him, “How can these things happen?”
verses.literal: Answered Nicodemus and said to Him; How are able these things to be?

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ διδάσκαλος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ταῦτα οὐ γινώσκεις;
verses.dgt: Jesus answered and said to him, “You are the teacher of Israel and you do not know these things?”
verses.literal: Answered Jesus and said to him; You yourself are the teacher the of Israel and these things not know?

verses.greek: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν, καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἡμῶν οὐ λαμβάνετε.
verses.dgt: Truly, truly, I say to you, we speak what we know and testify to what we have seen, yet you do not receive our testimony.
verses.literal: Amen Amen I say to you that what we know we speak and what we have seen we bear witness to, and the witness of us not you people receive.

verses.greek: εἰ τὰ ἐπίγεια εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια πιστεύσετε;
verses.dgt: If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
verses.literal: If the things earthly I have told you and not you believe, how if I may tell to you the things heavenly will you believe?

verses.greek: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.dgt: And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.
verses.literal: And no one has gone up into the heaven only except the One out of the heaven having come down, the Son the of Man
notes: The displayed SBLGNT ends with “the Son of Man.” The preserved TAGNT source includes the longer phrase “who is in heaven”; DGT follows SBLGNT here.

verses.greek: καὶ καθὼς Μωϋσῆς ὕψωσεν τὸν ὄφιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οὕτως ὑψωθῆναι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου,
verses.dgt: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
verses.literal: And even as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, thus to be lifted up it behooves the Son the of Man,

verses.greek: ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.dgt: so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.
verses.literal: so that everyone who is believing in Him may have life eternal.

verses.greek: Οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον ὥστε τὸν υἱὸν τὸν μονογενῆ ἔδωκεν, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν μὴ ἀπόληται ἀλλὰ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.dgt: For God loved the world in this way: he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
verses.literal: Thus for loved the God the world, that the Son the only begotten He gave, so that everyone who is believing in Him not may perish but may have life eternal.
notes: μονογενής is rendered “only” here, emphasizing the Son’s unique status; the word has traditionally also been rendered “only-begotten.”

verses.greek: οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν υἱὸν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα κρίνῃ τὸν κόσμον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα σωθῇ ὁ κόσμος διʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.dgt: For God did not send the Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
verses.literal: Not for sent the God the Son into the world that He may judge the world, but that may be saved the world through Him.

verses.greek: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν οὐ κρίνεται· ὁ δὲ μὴ πιστεύων ἤδη κέκριται, ὅτι μὴ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.dgt: The one who believes in him is not judged; but the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God.
verses.literal: The one believing on Him not is judged; the one but not believing already has been judged because not he has believed in the name of the only begotten Son the of God.

verses.greek: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ κρίσις ὅτι τὸ φῶς ἐλήλυθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον καὶ ἠγάπησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι μᾶλλον τὸ σκότος ἢ τὸ φῶς, ἦν γὰρ αὐτῶν πονηρὰ τὰ ἔργα.
verses.dgt: And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, because their deeds were evil.
verses.literal: This now is the judgement that the Light has come into the world, and loved the men rather the darkness than the Light; were for of them evil the deeds.

verses.greek: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ φαῦλα πράσσων μισεῖ τὸ φῶς καὶ οὐκ ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα μὴ ἐλεγχθῇ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
verses.dgt: For everyone who practices evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed.
verses.literal: Everyone for the evil practicing hates the Light and not comes to the Light so that not may be exposed the works of him;

verses.greek: ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα φανερωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ὅτι ἐν θεῷ ἐστιν εἰργασμένα.
verses.dgt: But the one who does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be revealed as having been done in God.
verses.literal: the one however practicing the truth comes to the Light that may be manifest his the works that in God have been done.

verses.greek: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν γῆν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διέτριβεν μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐβάπτιζεν.
verses.dgt: After these things Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and there he stayed with them and was baptizing.
verses.literal: After these things came the Jesus and the disciples of Him into the Judean land, and there He was staying with them and was baptizing.

verses.greek: ἦν δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων ἐν Αἰνὼν ἐγγὺς τοῦ Σαλείμ, ὅτι ὕδατα πολλὰ ἦν ἐκεῖ, καὶ παρεγίνοντο καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο·
verses.dgt: Now John also was baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people were coming and being baptized.
verses.literal: Was now also the John baptizing in Aenon near the Salim, because waters many were there. and they were coming and were being baptized;

verses.greek: οὔπω γὰρ ἦν βεβλημένος εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ὁ Ἰωάννης.
verses.dgt: For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
verses.literal: Not yet for were cast into the prison the John.

verses.greek: Ἐγένετο οὖν ζήτησις ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν Ἰωάννου μετὰ Ἰουδαίου περὶ καθαρισμοῦ.
verses.dgt: Then a dispute arose between John’s disciples and a Jew about purification.
verses.literal: Arose then a debate among the disciples of John with a certain Jew about purification.

verses.greek: καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ὃς ἦν μετὰ σοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ᾧ σὺ μεμαρτύρηκας, ἴδε οὗτος βαπτίζει καὶ πάντες ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτόν.
verses.dgt: They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, about whom you testified—look, he is baptizing, and everyone is coming to him.”
verses.literal: And they came to the John and said to him; Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you yourself have borne witness, behold He baptizes, and all are coming to Him.

verses.greek: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰωάννης καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐ δύναται ἄνθρωπος λαμβάνειν οὐδὲ ἓν ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.dgt: John answered and said, “A person cannot receive even one thing unless it has been given to him from heaven.”
verses.literal: Answered John and said; Nothing is able a man to receive and not one only unless it shall be given to him from the heaven.

verses.greek: αὐτοὶ ὑμεῖς μοι μαρτυρεῖτε ὅτι εἶπον· Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὁ χριστός, ἀλλʼ ὅτι Ἀπεσταλμένος εἰμὶ ἔμπροσθεν ἐκείνου.
verses.dgt: You yourselves testify for me that I said, ‘I am not the Christ, but I have been sent ahead of him.’
verses.literal: Yourselves you yourselves to me bear witness that I said Not am I myself the Christ, but for sent I am before Him.
notes: The preserved TAGNT wording contains additional words after “I said” that are not in the SBLGNT main text; the displayed Greek and DGT follow SBLGNT.

verses.greek: ὁ ἔχων τὴν νύμφην νυμφίος ἐστίν· ὁ δὲ φίλος τοῦ νυμφίου ὁ ἑστηκὼς καὶ ἀκούων αὐτοῦ, χαρᾷ χαίρει διὰ τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ νυμφίου. αὕτη οὖν ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ πεπλήρωται.
verses.dgt: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and listens to him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore this joy of mine has been fulfilled.
verses.literal: The one having the bride the bridegroom is. the now friend of the bridegroom, the one having stood and listening for him, with joy rejoices because of the voice of the bridegroom. This therefore the joy the of mine has been fulfilled.

verses.greek: ἐκεῖνον δεῖ αὐξάνειν, ἐμὲ δὲ ἐλαττοῦσθαι.
verses.dgt: He must increase, but I must decrease.
verses.literal: Him it behooves to increase, me myself however to decrease.

verses.greek: Ὁ ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν. ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς λαλεῖ· ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν·
verses.dgt: The one who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
verses.literal: The One from above coming above all is. The one being from the earth from the earth is and from the earth speaks. The One from the heaven coming above all is;

verses.greek: ὃ ἑώρακεν καὶ ἤκουσεν τοῦτο μαρτυρεῖ, καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει.
verses.dgt: What he has seen and heard, this he testifies, yet no one receives his testimony.
verses.literal: What He has seen and heard, this He testifies, and the testimony of Him no one receives.
notes: The preserved TAGNT source begins this verse with καί (“and”), which is absent from the SBLGNT main text; DGT follows SBLGNT.

verses.greek: ὁ λαβὼν αὐτοῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἀληθής ἐστιν.
verses.dgt: The one who has received his testimony has set his seal that God is true.
verses.literal: The one having received His the testimony has set his seal that the God true is.

verses.greek: ὃν γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ θεοῦ λαλεῖ, οὐ γὰρ ἐκ μέτρου δίδωσιν τὸ πνεῦμα.
verses.dgt: For the one whom God sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
verses.literal: He whom for sent the God, the declarations the of God speaks; not for by measure He gives the Spirit.
notes: The preserved TAGNT source explicitly has “God” as the subject of “gives,” while SBLGNT omits those words. DGT follows the shorter SBLGNT wording and leaves the subject implicit as “he.”

verses.greek: ὁ πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ τὸν υἱόν, καὶ πάντα δέδωκεν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.dgt: The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand.
verses.literal: The Father loves the Son and all things has given into the hand of Him.

verses.greek: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον· ὁ δὲ ἀπειθῶν τῷ υἱῷ οὐκ ὄψεται ζωήν, ἀλλʼ ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μένει ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
verses.dgt: The one who believes in the Son has eternal life; but the one who disobeys the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.
verses.literal: The one believing in the Son has life eternal; the one however not obeying the Son not will behold life, but the wrath the of God abides on him.
notes: ἀπειθῶν means “disobeying” or “refusing to obey,” providing a deliberate contrast with “believing” in the first half of the verse.
